To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a TP 53 germline variant in a proband with a family history of LFS and multiple primary tumors and that targeted next generation sequencing (NGS), a technology that allows for the simultaneous sequencing in one run of a large number of genes, is an efficient tool to identify the genetic background of patients with multiple primary tumors.
we identified a TP553 germline mutation by targeted NGS in a family with a severe susceptibility to multiple primary tumors.

we identified the germline TP53 mutation (c.525G>A, p.R175H) in a family with a severe cancer phenotype and that targeted next-generation sequencing is an efficient method for the identification of the germline mutations in LFS families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and genetic analysis of a family with LFS, in which the proband had 5 primary malignancies and a TP53 mutation was detected by NGS.
the clinical and molecular characterization of a family with LFS.
the clinical history of the proband who had 5 malignant tumors in the first 20 years of life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of targeted NGS is a powerful tool to identify genetic alterations in hereditary cancer families.
NGS is an important tool for the genetic analysis in families with a complex clinical picture and a heterogeneous phenotype.
targeted NGS is a useful tool to investigate families with a heterogeneous spectrum of cancer and a high probability of carrying a germline mutation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGS is a powerful tool for the identification of germline mutations in cancer predisposition syndromes.
targeted NGS is a useful tool for genetic testing in LFS families and for the identification of the TP53 mutations.

NGS technology represents a valid and reliable tool for the identification of genetic mutations in families with multiple primary tumors, even when the clinical phenotype is complex and heterogeneous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeted NGS can identify mutations in families with LFS and can help to identify the genetic background and the cancer risk for the relatives.
the use of a panel of 94 cancer-related genes by targeted NGS is a useful strategy in clinical practice for the identification of genetic alterations in patients with a high cancer risk.
NGS is an efficient approach for genetic analysis and can be a powerful tool for identifying mutations in families with heterogeneous phenotypes.
